02 · Project overview

One project, seven moves.

Central research question

Can culturally meaningful map icons help users recognize and discover traditional regional restaurants faster and with greater confidence?

03 · Research context

India's food changes with every region.

Food traditions are shaped by many layers. Tap one.

Outline of India (official boundary) for orientation. Pins mark the four states with a high-fidelity icon.

04 · Problem

Most restaurant map markers tell users where a restaurant is, not what cultural food experience it represents.

Generic icon

Restaurant
Standard map restaurant marker

+ cultural layer
Culturally adaptive icon

Restaurant + regional context + food identity

This is framed as a design opportunity and a research gap. Existing maps do carry cultural cues in other places, such as reviews, photos and cuisine filters. The question here is whether the marker itself can carry more meaning.

07 · Design process

Research first, then design, then test.

08 · Icon system

One pin, three layers.

Layers are separated from the supplied West Bengal high-fidelity icon. Drag a layer back into place, click it to snap it in, or press Assemble.

09 · Low-fidelity exploration

States and union territories, sketched.

Exploration → Iteration → Refinement

Sketches are the original research artefacts, not redrawn. Cue descriptions are read from the sketches.

10 · High-fidelity system

The cultural layer changes the meaning.

Base icon says“Restaurant.” Every pin looks the same, so region and food type are unknown until a user opens the listing.
Cultural icon says“Restaurant, and a regional food identity.” The fork and knife stay, and a cue adds context at a glance.

High-fidelity icons supplied so far: Punjab, Tamil Nadu, West Bengal and Kerala. Other regions remain in the low-fidelity archive above.

11 · A/B testing

Inside the pin, or on its outer layer?

Version A · inside the icon area Version B · outer layer

Both versions are rebuilt as crisp vectors from the supplied West Bengal icon. Version B matches the supplied design. Version A is a schematic of the concept, with the fish moved inside the icon area.

Which version did participants prefer in this design test?
